_comment: The world map: a grid of square tiles, each one kind of terrain (world/map.py). 'width' and 'height' are in tiles. 'seed': the same number always grows the same world; null grows a new one every time the game starts. The map is not yet tied to the game's rules: nobody walks on it and nothing is built on it.

generation._comment: Two fields of smooth noise, height and wetness, each 0 to 1, decide every tile. 'feature_size': how many tiles across a typical hill or wood is (bigger: broader, calmer land). 'octaves': layers of finer detail. 'edge_falloff': how strongly the land sinks toward the map's edge, so that the world ends in sea (0: no sea border). Height picks the terrain from 'levels', lowest first: the first whose 'below' is above the tile's height. Between the beach and the hills, wetness picks it from 'land' the same way; 'marsh' is wet ground no higher than 'marsh.below'. 'rivers': how many run from the high ground down to the sea, and how long one may get in tiles.

home._comment: Where the people live (the age's word for it, 'home' in its terms: camp, village, city...). It is put on open ground as near the middle of the map as can be found within 'near_water' tiles of a river, with 'clear' tiles of buildable ground on every side. 'marker': what marks it on the map when the fire is not shown.

camp._comment: How the camp is laid out around its fire, which burns on the home tile. 'spots': named places, as [east, south] tiles from the fire (each is put on the nearest free walkable tile): the 'store' where the shared goods lie, the 'workshop' where things are made, the 'council' ground where offices do their work. 'beds': everyone has a sleeping place of their own on a ring this many tiles from the fire ([nearest, farthest]). 'radius': someone within this many tiles of the fire is 'in camp': only there can they take from or put into the store. 'markers': how the text display draws the fire (burning and out) and the store.

travel._comment: People have bodies on the map and walk to wherever a thing is done (core/movement.py). 'life_hours_per_tile': how long one tile of open ground takes to cross, in hours of the day-night cycle (a terrain's 'move_cost' multiplies it; 0.035 = about 2 minutes). A trip out of camp takes the walk there, the work, and the walk back to the store: 'trip_work_share' is the share of a task's own 'life_hours' that is the work on the spot (the rest used to stand for the walk, which is now really walked). Work at a spot in camp takes the walk there plus all of its 'life_hours'.

places._comment: Kinds of place where things are done. A task says which with its 'place' (data/ages/<age>/occupations/, work.json); a recipe is made at 'workshop' and an office's work done at 'council' unless it says otherwise; anything else is done at 'camp'. A place is either a camp spot ('at': fire, store, workshop, council, bed = one's own sleeping place, by_fire = a tile next to the fire) or somewhere out on the map: a walkable tile of one of 'terrain' (any, if not given) whose walk from the fire is between 'min_distance' and 'max_distance' tiles of open ground; one of the 'nearest' such tiles is chosen (all of them in range, if not given). Places out on the map are trips: the person comes back to the store when done.

sites._comment: A place a Scout finds (work.json 'sites') lies where the Scout went looking: on ground of its kind (the site kind's 'place' in the age's work.json) whose walk from the fire is between these distances. Trips of that kind then walk to it.

zoom._comment: How big a tile is drawn, in rows of text (it is twice as many characters wide): the first is fully zoomed out. + and - step through them.

terrain._comment: Every kind of terrain. 'code': one character that stands for it in a saved map (each must differ). 'walkable': people can cross it. 'buildable': a structure can stand on it. 'move_cost': how slow it is to cross (1: open ground). 'fresh_water': drinkable. 'glyphs', 'color', 'background': how the text display draws a tile (two characters wide; several glyphs are mixed for texture); a graphical client uses its own art for each terrain key instead.

deep_water.name: Deep water
deep_water.description: Open sea: no crossing without a boat.

water.name: Shallows
water.description: Shallow water near the shore: wading is slow.

river.name: River
river.description: Running fresh water: good to drink, slow to ford.

plains.name: Plains
plains.description: Open grassland: easy to cross and to build on.

marsh.name: Marsh
marsh.description: Wet, reedy ground: slow going, and nothing stands on it.

deep_forest.name: Deep forest
deep_forest.description: Old, thick forest: hard to get through.

mountains.name: Mountains
mountains.description: Steep rock: very slow to climb.

peaks.name: Snowy peaks
peaks.description: The highest summits, under snow: no way across.
